cards.text: Friend, this is a hard chapter, so I'm going to tell it straight and walk through it with you. It starts with Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob. She goes out to visit the daughters of the land.
Shechem, son of Hamor the Hivite and prince of the region, sees her. He takes her and lies with her by force.

cards.question: After what he did, Shechem wants nothing more to do with Dinah.
The text says Shechem loves Dinah and speaks to her tenderly. Then he goes to his father Hamor. What does he tell him?

answers.text: Get me this girl as a wife
Send her back to her father

cards.text: Word reaches Jacob that Shechem has defiled his daughter Dinah. But his sons are out in the field with the livestock.

cards.question: Jacob hears the news about Dinah, but his sons are away in the field. What does Jacob do?

answers.text: Goes to the city gate himself
Packs up the camp to leave

cards.text: Meanwhile, Hamor comes to speak with Jacob. And Jacob's sons hear what happened and come back from the field.

cards.question: When Jacob's sons hear what Shechem did to their sister, they are filled with ___ and ___.
The text calls what Shechem did to Dinah an outrage in Israel, a thing that should not be done.

cards.text: Then Hamor makes his case to Jacob and his sons: "My son Shechem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife."

cards.question: Hamor doesn't stop at one wedding. What else does he offer Jacob's family?

answers.text: To intermarry and settle in the land
To leave the region in peace
To rule the city alongside him

cards.text: Then Shechem himself speaks to Dinah's father and brothers: "Grant me this favor, and I will give you whatever you ask."

cards.question: Shechem wants Dinah as his wife, so he tells her family, "Demand a high ___ and an expensive gift."

cards.text: Jacob's sons answer Shechem and Hamor. But the text tells us up front: because Shechem had defiled their sister, they answer deceitfully.

cards.question: The brothers say giving their sister to an uncircumcised man would be a disgrace. What condition do they set for Hamor's city?

answers.text: Hamor must give up the city

cards.question: If the condition is met, the brothers say they will dwell among Hamor's people and become one people.
And if Hamor's men won't agree to be circumcised, what do the brothers say they'll do?

answers.text: Go to war against the city

cards.text: The brothers' offer seems good to Hamor and his son Shechem. And Shechem, the most respected of all his father's household, doesn't hesitate.

cards.question: The text gives a reason Shechem doesn't hesitate to meet the brothers' condition. What is it?

answers.text: He is delighted with Jacob's daughter
He is afraid of Jacob's sons
His father orders him to do it

cards.text: So Hamor and Shechem go to the gate of their city to talk to the men there.

cards.question: At the city gate, how do Hamor and Shechem describe Jacob's family to the men of the city?

answers.text: They are at peace with us
They are too strong to fight

cards.text: Then comes the catch. Jacob's family will only agree to be one people with them if all their men are circumcised.

cards.question: To win the men of the city over, Hamor and Shechem bring up the newcomers' livestock and possessions.

cards.text: And it works. Every man who went out of the city gate listens to Hamor and Shechem, and every male of the city is circumcised.

cards.question: Three days later, while the men of the city are still in pain, two of Dinah's brothers take their swords. Who are they?

cards.text: Simeon and Levi go into the unsuspecting city, and they slaughter every male.

cards.question: Simeon and Levi spare Hamor and his son Shechem.
Before Simeon and Levi go away, who do they take out of Shechem's house?

cards.text: Then Jacob's other sons come upon the slaughter and loot the city. They take the flocks, the herds, the donkeys and everything else, in the city and in the field.

cards.question: The text gives a reason Jacob's other sons loot the city. What is it?

answers.text: Their father had told them to

cards.question: The brothers plunder everything in the houses. They carry off all the possessions, along with the city's ___ and ___.

cards.text: Then Jacob speaks to Simeon and Levi: "You have brought trouble upon me by making me a stench to the Canaanites and Perizzites, the people of this land."

cards.question: Jacob tells Simeon and Levi his family is few in number. What is he afraid the people of the land will do?

answers.text: Drive his flocks out of Canaan
Refuse to trade with his family

cards.question: How do Simeon and Levi answer their father Jacob?

answers.text: They ask if Shechem should have treated Dinah that way
They say they are sorry for the trouble
They promise to make peace with the land

cards.text: And the chapter ends right there, on a question hanging in the air. Stay with me, friend. Jacob's story isn't done yet.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "Demand a high ___ and an expensive gift.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Leaving out jokes is right for this passage, but most story cards are bare restatements of the verse with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. Examples are stop 1 cards 2, 5 and 7, and stop 2 cards 3, 9 and 12. Apart from the opening line and the last card, he never acts as the fatherly teacher who walks the baker through a hard moment or helps them see why it matters.

rule.text: **Short, but not stripped down.** A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "shame" is close to the brothers' reaction. In 34:14 they call it "a disgrace to us." A baker could argue that shame is part of how they felt.

rule.text: **No near-matches.** A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Go to war against the city" is true later in the passage, because Simeon and Levi attack the city in 34:25-26. Card 14 has already told the baker the brothers are answering deceitfully, so a baker could argue for this answer.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: This story card says Simeon and Levi "slaughter every male." That already answers the next choice card (card 10), which asks whether they spare Hamor and Shechem.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "horses" and "chariots" are animals and objects, while the right answers are people, so they are not the same kind of thing and the right answers stand out. Also, 34:28 says the brothers took "everything else in the city or in the field," so a baker could argue that "horses" is right.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question says Jacob is "afraid" as a fact. In 34:30 Jacob only says what could happen. The text never names his feeling.

rule.text: **Feelings:** He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has 10 choice cards, and 7 of them are multiple choice, with only 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The right answer says "treated Dinah that way," and no card ever gives the actual words of 34:31 ("like a prostitute"). The passage's last line loses its content and leans on a vague pointer. It seems to have been softened on purpose.
findings.question: In a passage about sexual violence, may Papa Dorin's cards use the BSB word "prostitute" from 34:31? The docs say "Always clean" and "kids can still play," but the goal is that the baker misses no important detail. Should the answer be rewritten to say what Simeon and Levi actually ask?
